description: Tiger Spiketail (Zoraena erronea) is a striking wildflower in the Spiketails family known for its distinctive striped petals and robust flowering spike. This New England native typically blooms in mid to late summer and serves as an important nectar source for regional pollinators.

idTips.label: Striped Petals
idTips.description: Look for the characteristic tiger-like orange and cream striped pattern on the flower petals that gives this plant its common name

idTips.label: Flowering Spike
idTips.description: The flowers are densely clustered along a prominent upright spike, creating a columnar inflorescence

idTips.label: Leaf Structure
idTips.description: Basal leaves are lance-shaped and form a rosette at the plant's base before the flowering stem emerges

habitat: Tiger Spiketail thrives in well-drained meadows, open woodlands, and rocky slopes throughout New England, preferring areas with full to partial sunlight.
funFact: The plant's scientific name Zoraena erronea refers to an early taxonomic confusion, as botanists initially misclassified it in a different genus before its true identity was established.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Delta-spotted Spiketails have more distinct, triangular yellow spots than the Twin-spotted Spiketail's paired round spots, and their spots are more numerous than the single large spots of Arrowhead Spiketails.

Twin-spotted Spiketails are distinguished from Delta-spotted Spiketails by having two round spots per segment rather than triangular markings, and from Tiger Spiketails by their smaller size and less bold yellow stripes.

Among its spiketail relatives, the Arrowhead Spiketail is distinguished by those distinctive arrow-shaped abdominal spots - Delta-spotted Spiketails have triangular spots that don't point directionally, while Twin-spotted Spiketails have paired round spots rather than arrows.
